tool.name: Normalize readouts
tool.command:
mkdir pycytominer_output &&
## Convert the input to CSV for pycytominer #if $profiles.ext in ["tsv", "tabular"] python '$__tool_directory__/format_converter_csvtsv.py' -i '$profiles' -o 'profiles.csv' -c tsv2csv && #else cp '$profiles' 'profiles.csv' && #end if
## Since the strata are input as integers, they need to be converted in a a comma separated string columns_headers=`head -n1 'profiles.csv' | cut -d, -f'$column'` &&
pycytominer normalize --profiles 'profiles.csv' --output_file './pycytominer_output/output.csv' --output_type 'csv' #if str($treatment) != 'all' --samples "\$columns_headers == '$treatment'" #else --samples 'all' #end if --method '$method' &&
## Convert the result back to TSV for the Galaxy dataset python '$__tool_directory__/format_converter_csvtsv.py' -i 'pycytominer_output/output.csv' -o '$output' -c csv2tsv

param.name: profiles
param.label: Input feature-readouts table
param.help: Table with features extracted from images, normally after annotation with treatments

param.name: column
param.label: Column with normalization values
param.help: Column containing the values to use for normalized (e.g., Metadata_treatment)

param.name: treatment
param.label: Value
param.help: Normalization reference (e.g., <tt>DMSO</tt>, <tt>Control</tt>). In cell painting, Z-scoring against <tt>DMSO</tt> control wells is the most common approach. Use <tt>all</tt> to normalize against the entire plate.

tool.help:
**Scales readouts to a common range and limits plate-to-plate technical variation.**
Documentation: https://pycytominer.readthedocs.io/en/stable/walkthroughs/pycytominer_cli.html#Step-3:-Normalize
